The model tells its story from the top down. Established physics comes first: seven extra dimensions curled into a special shape leave a four-dimensional world whose forces and fields are counted by the shape's holes. Next comes how the shape is chosen. A symmetry of the model's basic 3-form fixes how a seven-dimensional doughnut is folded, and Joyce's recipe for smoothing the folds gives a family of possible shapes. Only some of them have no loops that cannot be shrunk away, and among those only one lets the model's twelve links match the twelve smoothed creases one to one (the model identifies each link with one crease, an assumption it states openly). That shape has 4 two-dimensional holes and 24 three-dimensional holes, and counting the folds that leave creases gives 3 generations of particles. The model's own assumptions -- a 26-dimensional space with two time directions, split into two mirror halves joined by twelve links -- are labelled as assumptions. Four problems remain open: why matter tells left from right, what fixes the size of the extra dimensions, what drives dark energy, and why particles have the masses they do.

Instead of putting particles and forces into spacetime by hand, PM proposes that geometry comes from a fundamental field (the 'Pneuma') and that the shape of the seven hidden dimensions sets the particle content. The shape it uses is built by Joyce's method: a seven-dimensional doughnut folded by three mirror symmetries, with the creases smoothed out. Its hole counts are (b_2, b_3) = (4, 24), and the number of folds that leave creases gives 3 generations.

The pursuit of a unified description of the fundamental forces runs from Maxwell’s unification of electricity and magnetism through grand unification to Kaluza-Klein theory and M-theory on G₂ manifolds. This section follows that arc and then tells the model’s own story top down: the standard physics it uses; how its internal space Y<sub>7</sub> — Joyce’s resolution of T<sup>7</sup>/(ℤ/2)<sup>3</sup>, with (b<sub>2</sub>, b<sub>3</sub>) = (4, 24) — is selected without fitting; its postulates (a 26D bulk of signature (24,2) with one time per 13D(12,1) shadow, and twelve bridges); what its computations establish (CG.1–CG.11); what was corrected; and what remains open — chirality, moduli stabilisation, dark energy and flavour.

This paper presents Principia Metaphysica, a speculative model built on established physics — M-theory compactified on a compact seven-dimensional internal space — together with postulates of its own: a 26-dimensional bulk of signature (24,2), whose 24 space directions pair into twelve bridges and whose two times belong one to each of two 13-dimensional shadows of signature (12,1). The internal space is Y7, Joyce’s resolution of T7/(ℤ/2)3: a compact 7-manifold with a torsion-free G2-structure. Its Betti numbers are (b2, b3) = (4, 24); its fundamental group is trivial and χ(Y7) = 0. It is selected, not fitted. The model’s 3-form φ fixes the folding group Γ = (ℤ/2)3; Joyce’s construction from Γ reaches a family of 28 Betti pairs; a finite fundamental group occurs only on the line where all three folds are singular; and on that line the match between the 12 bridges and the 4 resolved singular components picks out Y7 without reference to data (§1.3.2). Three generations then follow as ngen = b2/4 = 3, the number of singular involutions — a count that the observed three generations test rather than choose. The introduction tells this story top down: the standard physics the model uses, how the geometry is selected, the model’s postulates, what its computations establish (the certificate CG.1–CG.11 of Section 2.4), what has been corrected, and what remains open. Four physics problems are open, and the geometry avoids none of them: chirality, moduli stabilisation (Re(T) included), dark energy and flavour. The model does not fit the data globally: the validation registry’s computed verdict is POOR_FIT, earlier global-alignment headlines are withdrawn, and each comparison with experiment is reported in its own row.

On that line the model’s own structure singles out one member. Its twelve bridges are the directed edges of K<sub>4</sub> on a Fano arc of four faces, grouped into three E<sub>8</sub> blocks. The three singular involutions fix such an arc, and each E<sub>8</sub> block contains exactly one side of their triangle, so blocks and involutions match one to one, and the twelve bridges match the twelve resolved components as a single 3 × 4 structure. That structure exists only on the all-plain members of the family, and on the n = 3 line the all-plain member is (b<sub>2</sub>, b<sub>3</sub>) = (12, 43) (CG.8). Working assumption WA-1 identifies each bridge with one resolved A<sub>1</sub> component, carrying one U(1); the author adopted it (ruling D-015), so the correspondence selects the member without data. Its consequence to test: the 4 U(1) gauge couplings come in three quartets, one per E<sub>8</sub> block.

The internal space is that member: Y<sub>7</sub> = Joyce’s resolution of T<sup>7</sup>/(ℤ/2)<sup>3</sup>, a compact 7-manifold with a torsion-free G<sub>2</sub>-structure, with (b<sub>2</sub>, b<sub>3</sub>) = (4, 24), Betti sequence (1, 0, 4, 24, 24, 4, 0, 1) and b<sub>3</sub> = 7 + 3b<sub>2</sub> = 7 + 12, π<sub>1</sub> = 1 and χ(Y<sub>7</sub>) = 0 (CG.1–CG.4). Its singular set is 4 disjoint flat three-tori, each with b<sub>1</sub> = 3; on the smooth manifold they carry U(1)<sup>4</sup> (SU(2)<sup>4</sup> at the orbifold point), with the local content of N = 4 super Yang–Mills (CG.3, CG.5). Three generations follow from the selection rather than choosing it: n<sub>gen</sub> = b<sub>2</sub>/4 = 3, the number of singular involutions. Each singular involution fixes one Γ-orbit of four three-tori, so b<sub>2</sub>/4 counts the singular involutions (CG.3). Earlier versions picked the seed by requiring three generations, which is selection by data; with WA-1 adopted, the seed is selected without data and three generations become an output tested against the three observed.

M-Theory on G₂ Manifolds (Acharya, Witten, et al. ~2000s–present)

M-theory on a compact G₂ manifold gives four-dimensional N = 1 physics; non-abelian gauge fields live on codimension-4 singularities and chiral fermions at codimension-7 conical points (Acharya & Witten 2001). PM draws on this literature — Joyce’s construction of compact G₂ manifolds, Acharya’s local super Yang–Mills on Joyce orbifolds (1999), the Lukas–Morris moduli Kähler potential (2004) and the flux analysis of Acharya, Denef and Valandro (2005) — and on Halverson & Morrison (2020) for the wider G₂ landscape. Earlier versions also used the twisted-connected-sum construction of Corti-Haskins-Nordström-Pacini (2015) and a KKLT-style racetrack (KKLT 2003, Blanco-Pillado et al. 2004). Both are off-path: Y7 is a Joyce orbifold resolution, b3 = 24 lies outside every published TCS range, and no racetrack exists on it (§1.3.5).

This section establishes the mathematical foundation of the Principia Metaphysica framework. We introduce the 26-dimensional action with signature (24,2) decomposing into dual 13D(12,1) shadows, each carrying its own timelike direction ((12,1) + (12,1) = (24,2)). Ghost control of the second time is OPEN: the appeal to Bars' Sp(2,R) ghost-freedom theorem is withdrawn (signature ruling 2026-08-31). We derive the 4D effective action through Kaluza-Klein dimensional reduction on Y₇, Joyce's resolution of T⁷/(ℤ/2)³ whose A₁ loci are resolved by Eguchi-Hanson patches, giving b₂ = 4 and b₃ = 24. (This abstract previously named a TCS — Twisted Connected Sum — G₂ manifold with h1,1=4 Kähler moduli sectors. That construction is off-path and kept as an exclusion: the twisted connected sum (retired reading) exhibits 71 ≤ b₃ ≤ 155, and b₃ = 24 lies outside that range, so TCS is recorded as an EXCLUSION rather than as this framework's construction.) The generation count n_gen = b₂/4 = 3 is the number of singular involutions; the earlier n_gen = b₃/8 route is abandoned. The moduli, Re(T) included, are OPEN on Y₇: G4 flux fixes none at leading order and no gaugino racetrack exists, so the racetrack value ε ≈ 0.2257 (from flux numbers N₁ = 24, N₂ = 23; canonical e^{-3/2} = 0.22313) is calibrated at the off-path seed b₃ = 24, not derived. The Pneuma-Vielbein bridge validates metric emergence from spinor bilinears with Lorentzian signature (-,+,+,+). On holonomy: phi is a G2-structure for the COMPACT real form. Hitchin's cubic construction gives an induced metric of signature (7,0), so a Riemannian G2-holonomy manifold is available and Joyce's construction applies.

On the adopted Y₇ the singular set is 4 A₁ loci, giving U(1)<sup>4</sup> on the resolution and SU(2)<sup>4</sup> at the orbifold point (CG.3, CG.5). Y₇ has no D₅ locus, so the SO(10) mechanism described here is the framework's model construction, not a property of Y₇. In that construction, SO(10) gauge symmetry arises from a D_5-type singularity, where the holonomy group can develop ADE-type singularities that enhance the gauge symmetry.

K_Pneuma is constructed as a Joyce orbifold T<sup>7</sup>/(ℤ/2)<sup>3</sup>, whose A₁ singular loci are resolved by Eguchi-Hanson patches [Joyce 2000, ch. 11-12]. On this seed the resolution count does NOT fix the topology, because the seed is off the reachable family: b₂ = 4 counts the A₁ T³ families, and b₃ = 24 is carried as an INPUT on the off-path seed seed_24: the resolution relation b₃ = 7 + 3b₂ would give 19 here, so this pair is not on the Joyce-reachable family at all. The Dimensional Descent Chain and Its Status: each step in the descent from 26D to 4D, with what supports it. (1) The 26D bulk of signature (24,2): a postulate — 24 space directions and one time per shadow; the earlier appeal to the bosonic critical dimension is withdrawn, because 26 is critical only for one time. (2) The 12 × (2,0) bridge pairs: the bulk’s 24 space directions taken in pairs, 24/2 = 12; each pair is Euclidean, and ghost control of the second time is open. (3) The dual 13D(12,1) shadows: OR reduction, proposed as the orientation-preserving projection consistent with spinor coherence ((R⊥full)² = I for 12 pairs). (4) Compactification on Y7: M-theory on a compact G2 manifold preserves N = 1 supersymmetry in 4D (standard; Joyce, 2000), and Y7 = Joyce’s resolution of T7/(ℤ/2)3, with (b2, b3) = (4, 24), is selected as the Introduction describes (§1.3.2). This paper presents Principia Metaphysica, a speculative model built on established physics — M-theory compactified on a compact seven-dimensional internal space — together with postulates of its own: a 26-dimensional bulk of signature (24,2), whose 24 space directions pair into twelve bridges and whose two times belong one to each of two 13-dimensional shadows of signature (12,1). What is standard, what is postulated, what is found

Standard physics is cited to its source; postulates are the model's own assumptions; findings are established by the computations above; corrections record what was wrong; open problems are stated as open.

M-theory on a compact 7-manifold with holonomy G2 gives 4D N = 1 supergravity with b_2 abelian vector multiplets and b_3 neutral chiral multiplets.
Curling up seven extra dimensions into a special shape called a G2 manifold leaves a four-dimensional world with a fixed set of force carriers and shape parameters, counted by the shape's holes.

Proof. Armstrong: pi_1 of the quotient is the orbifold group modulo the subgroup generated by elements with fixed points, and resolving A_1 loci does not change it. Along a coordinate fixed by every singular involution, the projection to Isom(R) kills that subgroup and sends the lattice translation to x -> x + 1, so pi_1 is infinite. With no such coordinate the singular involutions span Gamma and pi_1 = 1. Singular involutions are independent over F_2, so k = 2^(3-n) - 1 for n of them.

(CG.7) What Joyce's construction reaches from phi's (Z/2)^3

Joyce's construction from phi's diagonal (Z/2)^3 -- pairwise-disjoint singular sets, each family resolved by Eguchi-Hanson spaces with every admissible lift -- reaches 28 literature-checked pairs (b_2, b_3): n = 0: b_2 + b_3 = 7, b_2 = 0..0; n = 1: b_2 + b_3 = 23, b_2 = 0..8; n = 2: b_2 + b_3 = 39, b_2 = 4..12; n = 3: b_2 + b_3 = 55, b_2 = 8..16. The off-path seed b_3 = 24 is not among them. The computation reproduces Joyce's JDG II Example 4, b_2 = 8 + l, b_3 = 47 - l, by computing each family's contribution rather than looking it up. 8 further pairs arise only through lifts on order-8 stabilisers that no published example covers, and are not counted.

Proof. Enumerate every conjugacy class of half-shift actions of phi's diagonal (Z/2)^3; keep the pairwise-disjoint ones (Joyce's Condition 2.1.2); for each family compute the lift-character cohomology of T^3/Stab and sum over families and lifts. The result is checked against Joyce's JDG II Example 4 by computation, and matches an independent red-team enumeration.

items: Admissibility is Joyce's Condition 2.1.2: pairwise-disjoint singular sets. Then every singular point has isotropy {1, sigma}, and any further stabiliser of a fixed torus acts freely on it.

Summing over families and lifts, class by class, gives b_2 + b_3 = 7 + 16 n for n singular involutions.

(CG.5) Gauge content of Y_7
The active seed seed_24, (b_2, b_3) = (4, 24), is not reachable by the construction: no admissible assignment realises it, so nothing here derives it.

Proof. Acharya: M-theory on C^2/Gamma fibred over a 3-manifold M gives one gauge field, 2 b_1(M) scalars and 1 + b_1(M) fermions in the adjoint, the content of pure N = (1 + b_1) super Yang-Mills. Every locus here is a flat T^3 with trivial monodromy (y7-singular-components), so b_1 = 3 and the local theory is N = 4. On the resolution the 12 SU(2)s break to U(1)^12, with gauge kinetic functions T^7, T^6, T^5 by blow-up type (Lukas-Morris eq. 1.3).

(CG.11) The flux potential cannot accelerate the universe

Four moduli faces organise the Principia Metaphysica dual-shadow architecture: each face controls a distinct sub-sector of the compactified geometry, with the dominant face (T₁) governing the observable sector and the subdominant faces (T₂, T₃, T₄) governing progressively deeper shadow sectors. The octonionic decomposition of the 24-dimensional Leech vacuum partitions it as 24/8 = 3. The 24 here is dim(Λ₂₄), a lattice dimension — NOT the third Betti number, which is b₃ = 24 on the adopted seed. This abstract previously read "we prove that exactly three fermion generations arise ... a mathematical theorem, not a parameter fit". The arithmetic is exact and is kept; the claim that it SUPPLIES the generation count is withdrawn. The published count is n_gen = b_3 / 8 = 3.0. On the Joyce-reachable family b_3 is ODD at every profile and 8 divides no odd number, so this route yields an integer NOWHERE on the family -- not merely a wrong value at one point. Here b_3 = 24 is not on that family, so this route returns 3.0 only because the seed sits off it.

Modular invariance of the partition function Z(q) = η(τ)^{-n} requires the oscillator count to satisfy n ≡ 0 (mod 24); the minimal positive solution is n = 24, the exponent of η²⁴, the modular discriminant. The engine counts these oscillators with the bulk's 24 space directions. For the one-time bosonic string at signature (25,1), D = 24 + 2 = 26 is the critical dimension; the claim that the (24,2) bulk sits at its critical dimension is RETIRED (signature ruling 2026-08-31), since with two times the critical dimension is 27–28. The condition does not fix the internal topology: b₃ counts the 3-cycles of Y₇, b₃ = 24 on the live seed, which is 0 (mod 24). Reading n as b₃ was the off-path seed_24 identification and is withdrawn.

The partition function of the theory must be invariant under modular transformations τ → (aτ+b)/(cτ+d) with ad - bc = 1. For Z(q) = η(τ)^{-n} this constrains the oscillator count n; the engine counts the 24 oscillators with the bulk's 24 space directions. The signature ruling of 2026-08-31 records that no even self-dual lattice exists at (24,2), so a modular-invariance claim about the bulk needs its own footing. An earlier version identified n with b₃, one oscillator per associative 3-cycle of the internal manifold. That identification is withdrawn: b₃ = 24 on the live seed, so n = b₃ fails, and the constraint does not bear on the internal manifold's third Betti number.

The Dimensional Descent Chain and Its Status: each step in the descent from 26D to 4D, with what supports it. (1) The 26D bulk of signature (24,2): a postulate — 24 space directions and one time per shadow; the earlier appeal to the bosonic critical dimension is withdrawn, because 26 is critical only for one time. (2) The 12 × (2,0) bridge pairs: the bulk’s 24 space directions taken in pairs, 24/2 = 12; each pair is Euclidean, and ghost control of the second time is open. (3) The dual 13D(12,1) shadows: OR reduction, proposed as the orientation-preserving projection consistent with spinor coherence ((R⊥full)² = I for 12 pairs). (4) Compactification on Y7: M-theory on a compact G2 manifold preserves N = 1 supersymmetry in 4D (standard; Joyce, 2000), and Y7 = Joyce’s resolution of T7/(ℤ/2)3, with (b2, b3) = (4, 24), is selected as the Introduction describes (§1.3.2). (5) 4D physics: three generations are counted as ngen = b2/4 = 3, the number of singular involutions; how they become chiral is open, because Y7 has no codimension-7 points, and the earlier route through a Calabi–Yau sub-manifold of the twisted-connected-sum construction is off-path.

The model proposes that a condensate flux mismatch between the shadows produces a bridge pressure, ρbreath = |Tabnormal − R⊥ Tabmirror|, and that this residue drives cosmic acceleration. It is a proposal: dark energy is OPEN. The leading-order flux potential on Y7 cannot accelerate the universe (|∇V|/V ≥ 5√(2/7) ≈ 2.673 > √2, CG.11). The value w0 = −1 + 1/b3 = −23/24 once quoted here is frozen at the off-path seed b3 = 24 and has no derivation; both it and the adopted-seed value −23/24 lie more than 3σ from the DESI DR2 headline w0 = −0.752 ± 0.057.

Each shadow compactifies on the internal space Y<sub>7</sub> = Joyce’s resolution of T<sup>7</sup>/(ℤ/2)<sup>3</sup>: a compact 7-manifold with a torsion-free G<sub>2</sub>-structure, with (b<sub>2</sub>, b<sub>3</sub>) = (4, 24) (Introduction, §1.3.2; certificate in Section 2.4). Three generations are counted as n<sub>gen</sub> = b<sub>2</sub>/4 = 3, the number of singular involutions. The effective index χ<sub>eff</sub> = 48n = 144 (the K3 reading, adopted by the author’s ruling D-015) restates that count; it is not the Euler characteristic of Y<sub>7</sub>, which is 0. Earlier text called the manifold a ‘hard-lock’ that keeps the constants of nature from drifting; that is not supported, because the metric moduli of Y<sub>7</sub>, Re(T) included, are not fixed at leading order (CG.6).

The model proposes that vacuum energy is screened by flux through the 3-cycles of Y<sub>7</sub> (24 of them), with brane-tension cancellation inside them setting a small floor. It is a proposal, not a resolution of the cosmological-constant problem: the leading-order G<sub>4</sub>-flux potential on Y<sub>7</sub> is positive and runs away (CG.6) and cannot accelerate the universe (CG.11), so dark energy and the cosmological constant are open.

The model tells its story from the top down. Established physics comes first: seven extra dimensions curled into a special shape leave a four-dimensional world whose forces and fields are counted by the shape's holes. Next comes how the shape is chosen. A symmetry of the model's basic 3-form fixes how a seven-dimensional doughnut is folded, and Joyce's recipe for smoothing the folds gives a family of possible shapes. Only some of them have no loops that cannot be shrunk away, and among those only one lets the model's twelve links match the twelve smoothed creases one to one (the model identifies each link with one crease, an assumption it states openly). That shape has 4 two-dimensional holes and 24 three-dimensional holes, and counting the folds that leave creases gives 3 generations of particles. The model's own assumptions -- a 26-dimensional space with two time directions, split into two mirror halves joined by twelve links -- are labelled as assumptions. Four problems remain open: why matter tells left from right, what fixes the size of the extra dimensions, what drives dark energy, and why particles have the masses they do.

Instead of putting particles and forces into spacetime by hand, PM proposes that geometry comes from a fundamental field (the 'Pneuma') and that the shape of the seven hidden dimensions sets the particle content. The shape it uses is built by Joyce's method: a seven-dimensional doughnut folded by three mirror symmetries, with the creases smoothed out. Its hole counts are (b_2, b_3) = (4, 24), and the number of folds that leave creases gives 3 generations.

Start with a flat 7-dimensional torus. Of its 35 possible 3D direction-combinations, folding by the symmetry group leaves exactly 7 global 3D hallways intact. That is the constant 7. The folding pinches the space along 3-dimensional seams -- creases, each one a small 3D torus. Counting the independent families of seams gives b_2 = 4: each repaired seam family traps exactly one new 2D bubble. Physics cannot live on a crease, so each seam is repaired by gluing in a smooth patch (an Eguchi-Hanson space). Every repair spawns exactly 3 new independent 3D chambers along its seam. On this branch b_3 = 24 and b_2 = 4, and the assembly-line relation b_3 = 7 + 3 b_2 FAILS (it would give 19) -- which is one of the reasons this branch is off the constructible family.

The construction is a Joyce orbifold T^7/(Z/2)^3 with A_1 singularities resolved by Eguchi-Hanson patches: b2 = 4 counts one exceptional 2-class per resolved seam family, and b3 = 7 + 3 x 4 = 24 splits as 7 flat 3-forms plus 3 twisted 3-forms per family. The generation count is the number of singular involutions, n = 3 (the rank of their span); b2/4 recovers it only because this member is all-plain. The effective index chi_eff = 144 reads as one Kummer K3 (chi = 24) per singular involution in each of the two shadows -- the K3 reading, adopted 2026-10-01 (D-015).

The generation count is not adjustable: it is the number of singular involutions, fixed by the construction.
